code:
from pyspark.sql.types import IntegerType

trips = trips.withColumn(
  "passenger_count", col("passenger_count").cast(IntegerType())
)

# equivalent, with a string name:
trips = trips.withColumn(
  "passenger_count", col("passenger_count").cast("int")
)
caption: Both forms are equivalent — string name is shorthand, type class matches StructType.

code:
# fare_amount is a string column; one row contains "N/A"
trips.withColumn(
  "fare_amount", col("fare_amount").cast("double")
).show()

# The "N/A" row's fare_amount becomes NULL -- not an error
caption: PySpark favors null over crashing the whole job — a real place bad data hides.

code:
# inferSchema=True: guesses + casts automatically, on read
# explicit schema: states types up front
# .cast(): does it by hand, after the fact, one column at a time
caption: CSV has no real types at all until something casts it.
